_meta.source: https://github.com/Cyfrin/audit-checklist (Solodit's Aggregated Smart Contract Audit Checklist)
_meta.version_notes: This file is a curated starter subset. For the full ~3700-line, ~200-item checklist, fetch the live_json_url at audit start. The schema below matches the live file exactly.

category_object.data: array of subcategories OR check items

check_item.question: string - the imperative question to ask of the code
check_item.description: string - background explaining why this matters
check_item.references: array of URLs - real audit findings showing this issue

_meta.how_to_use: In Phase 3a, walk items relevant to the protocol type identified in Phase 1. Universal categories (Attacker's Mindset, Access Control, Arithmetic) apply to every audit. Protocol-specific categories (e.g., AMM, Lending) apply selectively.

data.description: Universal attack patterns to consider for every audit. Walk these items regardless of protocol type.

data.question: Is the withdrawal pattern (pull, not push) used to prevent denial of service?
data.description: Push-style refunds break for all users if any single recipient reverts. Pull-pattern lets each user claim independently.
data.remediation: Have users withdraw via a separate function rather than receiving in a loop.

data.question: How does the protocol handle tokens with blacklisting (e.g., USDC)?
data.description: If a blacklisted address is in a critical flow (recipient of a refund, member of a payout list), the entire flow can DOS.
data.remediation: Allow protocols to skip or replace blacklisted recipients; do not block on a single failed transfer.

data.question: Can an attacker force the protocol to process an unbounded queue?
data.description: Spamming small entries into a queue that must be processed in full causes DoS at gas-limit boundary.
data.remediation: Bound iteration, paginate, or use pull-style claims.

data.question: Does the protocol rely on `address(this).balance` or `token.balanceOf(this)` instead of internal accounting?
data.description: An attacker can directly transfer tokens to manipulate the protocol's view of its own holdings. Classic vault inflation attack.
data.remediation: Track balances in internal storage updated only by the protocol's own deposit/withdraw functions.

data.question: Are 'get-or-create' patterns protected against front-running?
data.description: If a function creates a resource and then uses it, an attacker can front-run with different parameters and manipulate the eventual interaction.
data.remediation: Separate creation from use, or require the caller to pass the expected resource state and validate.

data.question: If commit-reveal is used, is it bound to the user and transaction parameters?
data.description: A commit-reveal scheme that doesn't bind to the user's address can be front-run by copying the commit.
data.remediation: Hash should include msg.sender, all parameters, and a per-user nonce.

data.question: Is read-only reentrancy possible via view functions called by other protocols?
data.description: External integrators reading a view function during a callback can see inconsistent state and act on it. ReadOnlyReentrancy was the Curve incident pattern.
data.remediation: Extend reentrancy guards to view functions whose return values are consumed by external integrators, or document the constraint.

data.question: Are state changes made before all external calls (Checks-Effects-Interactions)?
data.description: External calls can re-enter; if state is updated after the call, the re-entered call sees stale state.
data.remediation: Apply CEI strictly. Use ReentrancyGuard as a backup, not the primary defense.

data.question: Are ERC777 / ERC1155 / ERC721 callbacks considered as reentrancy vectors?
data.description: Tokens with hooks (ERC777 tokensReceived, ERC1155 onReceived, ERC721 onERC721Received) can re-enter on transfer. Many 'standard ERC20' protocols break with ERC777.
data.remediation: Either reject hook-supporting tokens, apply CEI, or use reentrancy guards on every function that transfers.

data.question: Is any price calculated from token balance ratios in a pool?
data.description: Direct balance-ratio pricing is flash-loan-manipulable. This has caused dozens of DeFi exploits.
data.remediation: Use Chainlink (or equivalent decentralized oracle) for asset prices; if using a DEX, use TWAP, not spot.

data.question: Is price read from a DEX spot (e.g., Uniswap V3 slot0)?
data.description: Spot prices from DEXes are manipulable in a single transaction via flash loan.
data.remediation: Use TWAP with a window appropriate to liquidity and volatility.

data.description: Universal. Verify every privileged function has correct authorization.

data.question: Does every state-changing function have appropriate access control?
data.description: Missing modifiers are the #1 cause of catastrophic exploits.
data.remediation: Apply onlyOwner, onlyRole, or explicit msg.sender checks. Audit every external/public non-view function.

data.question: Are role grants and revocations themselves access-controlled?
data.description: AccessControl misconfigurations (DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE not held by trusted entity) brick or compromise the protocol.
data.remediation: Verify the admin role hierarchy at deployment and any role-change paths.

data.question: Is `initialize()` protected against being called twice or by anyone?
data.description: Front-running deployment-then-initialize lets an attacker seize ownership.
data.remediation: Use OpenZeppelin Initializable; deploy and initialize atomically.

data.question: Are there any tx.origin checks for authorization?
data.description: tx.origin is phishable via intermediate contracts.
data.remediation: Always use msg.sender.

data.description: Universal. Even with Solidity 0.8+ overflow checks, precision and rounding bugs are common.

data.question: Are all `unchecked { }` blocks justified and bounded?
data.description: Developers often use unchecked for gas, but if assumptions break, overflow returns.
data.remediation: Comment why each unchecked is safe; verify the bound holds.

data.question: Does division happen before multiplication?
data.description: Integer division truncates; doing it before multiplication causes precision loss.
data.remediation: Multiply first, divide last. Use FixedPointMathLib or PRBMath for non-trivial math.

data.question: Are rounding directions correct (in protocol's favor for shares, against user for owed amounts)?
data.description: Rounding the wrong way creates dust loss for the protocol or free value for users. Inflation attacks exploit this.
data.remediation: Round shares down on deposit, up on withdraw. Round debt up against the borrower.

data.question: Are decimal differences handled correctly when comparing/combining tokens?
data.description: Comparing 6-decimal USDC to 18-decimal DAI without normalization breaks logic.
data.remediation: Always normalize to a single precision before arithmetic.

data.description: Universal. External calls are reentrancy and DOS vectors.

data.question: Are return values from low-level calls (call, send, transfer) checked?
data.description: Unchecked calls silently fail and proceed.
data.remediation: Always check the bool return; revert on failure unless intentional.

data.question: Is gas forwarded explicitly considered?
data.description: transfer/send forward 2300 gas, which has broken with EIP-2929 repricings. Hardcoded gas in call() can underflow with future repricings.
data.remediation: Use call{value: x}("") with checked return, no hardcoded gas, plus reentrancy guard.

data.question: Are external calls in loops protected against single-recipient DoS?
data.description: One reverting recipient blocks the whole loop.
data.remediation: Try-catch the call, or use pull-pattern.

data.description: Load if any oracle (Chainlink, Pyth, custom, DEX-derived) is used.

data.question: Is the oracle's staleness check enforced (heartbeat + updatedAt)?
data.description: A frozen oracle returning stale prices can cause incorrect liquidations or mints.
data.remediation: Require updatedAt within heartbeat; revert on stale.

data.question: Is the oracle's `answeredInRound` validated?
data.description: Chainlink can return data from a previous round if the latest round is incomplete.
data.remediation: Require answeredInRound >= roundId.

data.question: Is min/max price boundary respected (Chainlink aggregator)?
data.description: Chainlink aggregators clamp at min/max; LUNA crashed below the min price and the oracle returned the floor.
data.remediation: Check returned price against min/max from the aggregator and revert if at the boundary.

data.question: Is L2 sequencer uptime checked on Optimism, Arbitrum, Base?
data.description: If sequencer is down, oracle data is stale by definition; liquidations during downtime are unfair.
data.remediation: Use the L2 sequencer uptime feed; pause price-dependent ops during downtime + grace period.

data.question: If the oracle is custom or DEX-derived, is it manipulation-resistant?
data.description: Custom oracles often inherit DEX spot vulnerabilities.
data.remediation: Use TWAP, ensure deep liquidity, document the manipulation cost.

_extension_note: This starter contains the universal categories. For protocol-specific items (ERC20, ERC4626, AMM, lending, etc.), consult the corresponding files in references/protocols/, which were written to complement (not duplicate) this checklist. For the comprehensive ~200-item live checklist, fetch from live_json_url and grep by category.
